summary: 61.2% of frames are VXLAN-encapsulated (1722/2813) - APM receives outer tunnel headers instead of inner application traffic, blinding transaction analysis.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker is forwarding VXLAN-encapsulated traffic without stripping the overlay header. 61.2% VXLAN indicates SPAN/tunnel termination is not being decapsulated at the visibility layer before delivery to the APM port.
findings.impact_on_tool: APM cannot parse inner Ethernet/IP/TCP headers and application transactions; latency, error-rate and service-map calculations fail or are attributed to tunnel endpoints instead of real services. Despite needs_full_payload=false, the tool still needs decapsulated headers.

recommended_fix.why: Strip VXLAN header on the packet broker and forward only the inner frame so the 10G APM receives native traffic it can decode for APM transaction correlation.
